description: Question: in March 2025 the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) reported that dark energy may be weakening: the cosmological constant of the standard model, ΛCDM, fits its map of 14 million galaxies and quasars less well than a dark energy that changes with time. How strong is that, and which data carry it? And is the "Hubble tension" the same problem? Data: DESI DR2's BAO distances (seven redshift bins, 13 numbers with their covariance; DESI collaboration via the Cobaya likelihood repository), the 1,701 type Ia supernovae of Pantheon+ with their SH0ES Cepheid calibration (Scolnic et al. 2022, Brout et al. 2022), and Planck's acoustic angle θ* and sound horizon. Steps: a flat universe of matter, radiation and dark energy with w(z) = w0 + wa·z/(1+z), integrated for 21 × 41 × 53 values of Ωm, w0 and wa (w0 + wa < 0); for each, the χ² of the BAO (scale c/(H0·r_d) fitted analytically), of the supernovae (their absolute brightness left free, Hubble-flow sample binned in 36 log-redshift bins), and of the CMB as one more distance, to z = 1090; then ΛCDM against the best (w0, wa) per combination, and H0 from the supernovae with Cepheid distances against H0 from the sound-horizon ruler. Aha: each ruler alone is consistent with ΛCDM (BAO 1.7σ, supernovae 0.3σ), but their allowed bands cross away from it: together ΛCDM is off by 2.7σ (Δχ² 10.2), best w0 ≈ −0.87, wa ≈ −0.3, close to DESI's own 2.8σ for DESI + CMB + Pantheon+ (w0 = −0.84, wa = −0.62 in their full analysis). The signal sits at z ≈ 0.5–0.7, where DESI's expansion rate runs 3% above ΛCDM. The Hubble tension is a separate fault line: the distance ladder gives H0 = 73.2 km/s/Mpc (statistical error only), the sound-wave ruler with Planck's r_d gives 68.8, Planck's ΛCDM 67.4 ± 0.5; changing late dark energy doesn't close it. Caveats: supernova errors are diagonal (the published 1,701 × 1,701 covariance with systematics isn't used), which makes them look stronger than they are; the CMB here is θ* alone, a weak stand-in for the full Planck likelihood (so BAO+CMB gives 1.5σ against DESI's 3.1σ); radiation and r*/r_d are fixed approximations; the grid is coarse (steps 0.01, 0.03, 0.08); the significance depends on which supernova sample is used (DESI: 2.8σ with Pantheon+, 4.2σ with DES-Y5). Next: hover any point; read a combination's Δχ² in the verdict table; drill into one BAO bin's tracer; expand to the DES-Y5 or Union3 supernovae, or the full CMB distance priors.
name: Is dark energy weakening? DESI, supernovae and the Hubble tension
